name: manual_92d4ae
claim: When a fix has to be applied to more than one copy of the 'same' logic to actually work (e.g. patching a bug in 3+ near-identical files), treat that as a signal the duplication itself is the bug, not just today's instance of it -- propose consolidation to a single source of truth rather than accepting 'we fixed all the copies' as the resolution. Feature flags are the wrong tool for this: they solve toggleable runtime behavior, not accidental implementation drift that should never have diverged.

decisions.notes: PT's scripts/agent_coordination_core.py and _legacy.py were 94-98% byte-identical (verified two ways: context-diff line count and --no-index --numstat), with _core.py's only real value (a ReorderBuffer dedup fix, --seq claim support) buried inside a full duplicate rather than expressed as a diff. A third file, _phases.py, was orphaned dead code carrying a 4th copy of the same PhaseState/_phase_list logic. Today's phase-sort-key crash needed the same fix applied to all three living copies to actually reach the real CLI path -- a clear signal to consolidate, not just patch again next time.
